regionalNotesEnglish: Qualified fall-protection review is required for anchorage, lifeline setup, clearance, rescue, and the exact English safety source before release.
France/Québec terms for competent person, lifeline and fall clearance need qualified regional review.
archivedDraft.status: separate unapproved draft; no answer, audio or progress inheritance

sourceDecisionQuestions.question: Anchor/anchorage, lifeline, lanyard and fall distance need exact site-system and French technical senses. Archived distance libre de chute can mean fall clearance rather than source fall distance; Reader 6 adds required clearance absent from the source. Confirm terms with qualified roofing/fall-protection and dictionary reviewers.

The source says use the roof anchor without stating it is approved, and declares the anchor unsafe before the inspection. Archived French adds approuvé to card 10 and softens unsafe to semble dangereux in card 11/Reader 3. Preserve the source claims as evidence; a qualified safety/source reviewer must decide the approved site-specific wording before selection.
Competent person is a defined site role. Archived personne compétente is only conditional until the applicable jurisdiction, designation, inspection authority and clearance wording are confirmed.

The source asks for lifeline damage check and confirmation of the anchor setup before continuing. Archived French turns the latter into a request to have someone confirm it, and may imply inspection or safe return without a documented result. Resolve the site-specific sequence and source meaning before scoring or audio.

Archived speaking adds checking equipment, fall clearance and the rescue plan beyond the source's stop-work and competent-person setup confirmation. Keep these as internal domain review notes, not learner script or authoritative site procedure.
